explanation: Used matched plain/correct-guess/wrong-guess activations across facts, phrasings, and answer positions. The dominant copying signal emerged in layer 11 attention. A rank-one update uses a regularized guess-context direction, protected against plain-prefix means and recorded reply-start inputs, to steer the pre-RMSNorm output toward a neutral plain-question template at a magnitude sufficient to substantially attenuate copying. A smaller rank-eight layer-12 update reduces numerical copying modes while preserving shared response-format directions. All construction used closed-form activation statistics, SVDs, and local effects on unedited module inputs; no gradients, optimizers, or edited-model forward passes were used.
